echinochimaera-curva:abstract:1.title: Five new holocephalan ichthyodorulites from the Viséan (Middle Mississippian) St. Louis Formation of Indiana, USA, including the fin spine of a new echinochimaerid (abstract)

facts.statement: The species lived during the Viséan stage of the Carboniferous period.
Its type locality is the St. Louis Formation in Indiana, United States.
Echinochimaera is a genus of extinct holocephalan fish that lived in the Lower Carboniferous about 355 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió en el Carbonífero Inferior, hace unos 355 millones de años

facts.statement: Members of the genus reached less than 30 cm in length.
facts.quote: Llegaba a medir menos de 30 cm de largo

facts.statement: They had a rounded body, large pectoral fins, two dorsal fins (one with a mobile spine), and a paddle‑shaped tail, indicating a slow swimming lifestyle and likely non‑predatory habits.
facts.quote: Tenía un cuerpo redondeado, grandes aletas pectorales y dos aletas dorsales, dotada una de ellas una espina móvil. La forma de su cuerpo y sus aletas, así como la cola en forma de paleta, indican que este animal era un nadador lento, y probablemente no era un depredador.

facts.statement: A fin spine from the Viséan St. Louis Formation was provisionally referred to Echinochimaera and named Echinochimaera curva sp. nov.
The fin spine resembles that of Echinochimaera meltoni, suggesting it may belong to the same family.
If the spine truly belongs to an echinochimaerid, it would represent the earliest known member of the group.
The genus Echinochimaera ranges from 326.9 to 323.6 million years ago in the Serpukhovian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Serpukhovian to Serpukhovian (326.9 to 323.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Echinochimaera is placed in the family Echinochimaeridae within the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: Echinochimaera curva is a newly named species described in 2026 by Itano.
